question:
Three congruent circles with centers \(P,\) \(Q\) and \(R\) are tangent to the sides of rectangle \(ABCD\) as shown. The circle centered at \(Q\) has diameter \(4\) and passes through points \(P\) and \(R.\) The area of the rectangle is

[Figure 1](figures/1995_AMC_8_Q09_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The circles are congruent, so each has radius \(4\div2=2\). Since \(P\) and \(R\) lie on the circle centered at \(Q\),
\[
PQ=QR=2.
\]
Each circle touches both the top and bottom of the rectangle. A radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to that side, so the rectangle's height is one diameter, \(4\). These tangencies also place all three centers on the line midway between the top and bottom, in the order \(P,Q,R\) shown.

The left side is one radius to the left of \(P\), and the right side is one radius to the right of \(R\). Thus the width is
\[
2+PQ+QR+2=2+2+2+2=8.
\]
The rectangle's area is therefore
\[
4\times8=\boxed{32}
\]
square units, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
